## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

response.rationale: These look like two different concepts. Booking is kept in BookingRepository (`private readonly bookings = new Map<string, Booking>();`). The methods that call that repository suggest it is an individual booking for a session: it goes through payment (BookingService.handlePaymentResult), it can expire (BookingService.releaseExpired), it counts toward session availability (SessionService.availability), and it can be cancelled through IceMonitorService. ClubBooking has its own type (`create(input: NewClubBooking): ClubBooking`), its own service and its own repository, ClubBookingRepository, which it looks up by date and by month. That looks like a club reserving time slots, not a single customer's paid booking. The two share no code, have different lifecycles and are stored separately. They are related kinds of reservation, but they appear to model different business things.
